previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with malaise and burning dysuria, concerned about a recurrent MRSA UTI. Evaluation revealed chronic bacterial colonization of the urinary tract due to a long-term indwelling Foley catheter, not an acute infection. He had no fever, leukocytosis, or sepsis. The Foley catheter was replaced, and a single dose of antibiotics was given overnight, but further treatment was avoided to prevent resistance. Pyridium and Tylenol were started for symptom relief. His shortness of breath resolved, requiring no oxygen by the next day. Imaging showed no acute chest process or DVT. He remained stable, was educated on colonization versus infection, and was discharged home with services and follow-up arranged with primary care, cardiology, and urology.
